meta.titre: Meal Planning for the Family: Factors, Budget and Kitchen Time
meta.sous_theme: Factors in menu planning, budgeting and time plans

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Every evening a mother in Bamenda must decide what to cook with the money in her purse. A meal bought in a hurry is often costly and unbalanced, while a planned menu feeds everybody well for less money. This is why the GCE tests the factors that guide meal planning, how to share a budget, and how to organise work in the kitchen so that the food is ready on time.

items: A balanced meal contains energy foods, body-building foods and protective foods.
People of different ages and activities need different amounts of nutrients.
Food prices change with the season and the market.

sections.titre: Planning family meals: factors, principles and kitchen time
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What meal planning is
Meal planning means deciding in advance what the family will eat during a day or a week so that the meals are balanced, attractive, affordable and ready on time. It avoids waste and last-minute buying.

### Factors to consider

| Factor | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Nutritional needs (age, sex, activity, health, pregnancy) | A growing child, a pregnant woman and a heavy manual worker need different amounts of nutrients and energy; a sick or elderly person may need light, soft food. |
| Money available (income, budget) | It decides the quality and quantity of food; cheaper foods such as beans can replace costly ones. |
| Season and availability | Foods in season are fresher and cheaper. |
| Time, skill and equipment | A busy family needs quick dishes; the cook must be able to use the fuel and utensils at hand. |
| Likes, dislikes, religion and customs | A meal that is refused is wasted; allergies and food rules must be respected. |
| Number of people and the occasion | Quantities and the style of service change for a festival or a school day. |
| Storage facilities | A fridge or freezer allows food to be bought in larger amounts. |

### Principles of a good menu
- Include an energy food, a body-building food and a protective food (fruit or vegetables) in the day's meals.
- Give variety of colour, flavour and texture, and do not repeat the same cooking method for every dish.
- Keep to the budget and use up leftovers safely.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for advantages of managing time, or how to organise the work before a meal.
When asked to name or describe the document used to prepare a particular dish.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A recipe is a written set of instructions for preparing one dish. It gives the name of the dish, the list of ingredients with exact quantities, the method in order, the cooking temperature and time, and the number of portions. Following a recipe gives the same good result each time and helps to calculate the cost. A recipe is for one dish; a menu is the list of all the dishes in a meal.

sections.enonce_markdown: A family of six (two adults, a teenage boy, two school children and a grandmother) has $4\,800$ FCFA to spend on tomorrow's lunch. (a) State three factors that will guide the choice of the meal. (b) Calculate the amount available per person. (c) Plan a balanced lunch and show that its cost is within the budget (the prices are assumed for this question). Prices: rice $1\,200$ FCFA, beans $1\,100$ FCFA, leafy vegetables, tomatoes and onions $700$ FCFA, ripe plantain $900$ FCFA, pawpaw $600$ FCFA.

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "State" asks for short points; "calculate" needs a working line; "plan" needs a menu with a check against the money.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Three short factors, one division, one menu with a total.

etapes.action: Choose three factors that fit this family.
etapes.justification: The family has people of different ages and a fixed sum of money.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Nutritional needs of each age group. 2. Money available. 3. Food likes and dislikes (or time available for cooking).

etapes.action: Divide the budget by the number of people.
etapes.justification: Cost per person = total money divided by the number of persons.
etapes.resultat_markdown: $4\,800 \div 6 = 800$ so each person can spend **$800$ FCFA**.

etapes.action: Choose foods from each group and add their prices.
etapes.justification: The menu must have energy food (rice, plantain), body-building food (beans) and protective food (vegetables, pawpaw).

etapes.action: Compare the total with the budget.
etapes.justification: A good plan never spends more than the money available.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **(a)** Nutritional needs of the different ages; money available; likes and dislikes. **(b)** $4\,800 \div 6 = 800$ FCFA per person. **(c)** Menu: rice with a bean stew containing leafy vegetables, tomatoes and onions, with fried or boiled ripe plantain and pawpaw for dessert. It has energy, body-building and protective foods, and costs $4\,500$ FCFA, which is within the $4\,800$ FCFA available.

items.erreur_markdown: "Meal planning is only about having enough money."
items.pourquoi_faux: Money is one factor, but nutritional needs, season, time, skill, customs and the number of people also decide the menu.
items.correction_markdown: Name the factor and say why it matters, for example: age and activity change the nutrients a person needs.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "it saves time" as an advantage of time management in the kitchen.
items.pourquoi_faux: This only repeats the words of the question, so it earns no mark.
items.correction_markdown: Give a result: food is served hot and on time; fuel is not wasted; food is not burnt.

items.erreur_markdown: Planning fried fish, fried plantain, fried yam chips and fried doughnuts for one meal.
items.pourquoi_faux: The meal has no variety of cooking method, texture or colour, is high in fat, and has no protective food.
items.correction_markdown: Mix methods (for example grilled fish, boiled yam, a vegetable sauce) and add fruit or vegetables.

items.erreur_markdown: Spending the whole budget on meat and leaving nothing for fruit and vegetables.
items.pourquoi_faux: The meals become unbalanced and the protective foods that guard health are missing.
items.correction_markdown: Share the money between all food groups; cheaper proteins such as beans or eggs can replace part of the meat.

items.erreur_markdown: Confusing a recipe with a menu.
items.pourquoi_faux: A recipe gives ingredients and method for one dish; a menu lists the dishes that make up a meal.
items.correction_markdown: Say that the document with ingredients, quantities and method is a recipe.

items.enonce_markdown: State four pieces of information normally found in a recipe.
items.solution_markdown: Any four of: the name of the dish; the list of ingredients; the quantities of each ingredient; the method in steps; the cooking temperature and time; the number of portions it makes. (Award a mark for each correct item.)

items.enonce_markdown: A family of four has a weekly food budget of $28\,000$ FCFA. (a) Calculate the amount available for each day. (b) Calculate the amount for each person each day. (c) The mother plans to spend 40% of the day's money on lunch. How much is that for the whole family and for one person?
items.solution_markdown: (a) $28\,000 \div 7 = 4\,000$, so **$4\,000$ FCFA per day**. (b) $4\,000 \div 4 = 1\,000$, so **$1\,000$ FCFA per person per day**. (c) $\frac{40}{100} \times 4\,000 = 1\,600$, so lunch costs **$1\,600$ FCFA** for the family and $1\,600 \div 4 = 400$, that is **400 FCFA per person**.

items.enonce_markdown: Rice and a stew must be served at 13:00. The stew needs 40 minutes of cooking and the rice 25 minutes. Preparation (washing, peeling and chopping) takes 30 minutes and must be finished before any cooking starts. Two burners are available. (a) At what time should the stew go on the fire? (b) When should the rice go on? (c) At what time should preparation begin? (d) Explain why the stew is started first.
items.solution_markdown: (a) 13:00 minus 40 minutes: the stew goes on at **12:20**. (b) 13:00 minus 25 minutes: the rice goes on at **12:35**. (c) Preparation must end when the stew goes on, so it begins 30 minutes earlier, at **11:50**. (d) The stew takes the longest time to cook, so it must be started first for all the dishes to be ready together at the time of serving.

items_markdown: Factors in meal planning: nutritional needs, money, season, time and skill, likes and customs, number of people and occasion, storage.
A good menu has energy, body-building and protective foods, with variety of colour, flavour, texture and cooking method.
Budget work: total money divided by the number of days or persons gives the amount to spend.
Time management: work backwards from serving time, start the longest dish first, prepare before cooking; give specific advantages, not "it saves time".
A recipe is the written ingredients, quantities and method for one dish; a menu lists the dishes of a meal.
